 Porsche Expands 'Do Not Drive' Recall For Performance Models With Center-Lock Wheels That Could Fall Off
 By   Logan K. Carter 
 Oct. 25, 2026 2:25 pm EST 
 Porsche 
 Add Jalopnik on Google: 
 Preferred Source 
 Google Discover 
 The recalls have really been flowing lately, and not always from the automakers you might expect ( Ahem, Ford .) In truly rare form, Germany's crown jewel Porsche expanded a 2024 recall to include an additional 548 of its highest-performing cars, because their center-lock wheels might fall off. What sounds like a movie plotline to take out some of the wealthy elite is actually an unfortunate supplier defect, as the NHTSA Recall Report  states.
 The latest batch of Porsches involved in this recall include the 2024 911 Turbo (13 cars), 2024 911 S/T  (39 cars), 2024 911 GT3 RS (41 cars), 2024 911 GT3 (50 cars), 2024 718 Spyder RS (70 cars), 2024 718 Cayman GT4 RS (73 cars), 2024 911 Turbo S (94 cars), and 2024 911 GTS (168 cars). Porsche says owners of these cars should not drive them until a Porsche dealer has checked the center-lock wheel fastening system and replaced any out-of-specification parts.
 Porsche 
 The original recall issued almost exactly three years ago on October 28, 2024, included 1,851 2024 911 Turbos and 718 GT4 RS and Spyder RS models, so now a total of 2,399 cars are affected. 100% of those cars included in the first recall were estimated to be affected by the fault, but just 1.4% of the cars included in the new recall are expected to be affected.
 Owners should notice vibration before their wheel falls off
 Porsche 
 Fortunately, Porsche says immediate vibration should be perceptible if the center lock fractures on anyone's car, so if you're driving a 2024 Porsche sports car that suddenly starts vibrating, you might want to pull over as soon as possible.
 Porsche is aware of several incidents attributable to center lock fractures, and the only description of the cause provided says, "analyses of the affected material batch confirmed lead and bismuth contents outside the specification." The only other mentions of the issue say "...the center wheel lock components used in the center wheel fastening system within certain production ranges were manufactured out of specification."
 The latest do-not-drive warning arose after two additional field accidents involving fractured center lock components earlier this year in May and August, though no injuries were reported. Owners needn't worry about reimbursement for the repairs, since all affected cars are still covered under their warranty. Owners will be contacted by phone, email, and MyPorsche App push notifications by December 15, though VINs are already searchable on NHTSA's website.
